channel.title: DevPulse · Cloud & infra
channel.description: Daily cloud & infra stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Cloudflare Traces follows requests across platform operations and origins
item.description: Cloudflare Traces adds request timelines across supported security rules, transformations, cache decisions, routing, Workers, and origin handling, with sampling controls and OTLP export. Engineers can trace failures across platform boundaries without relying on a single service’s telemetry.

item.title: Quick Tunnels can restrict access with accountless email verification
item.description: Starting with cloudflared 2026.9.3, Quick Tunnels can use --allowed-mail to limit visitors to chosen addresses or domains, verified by a one-time PIN without requiring either side to have a Cloudflare account. This adds a practical access-control option for sharing local development services, including agent-built projects.

item.title: GKE CPU startup boost raises pod CPU during initialization without restarting containers
item.description: The preview feature uses the Vertical Pod Autoscaler to increase CPU during container startup and return allocation to its baseline after readiness, without a restart. It targets cold-start delays and the cost of sizing requests for brief CPU peaks.

item.title: Cloudflare adds an OHTTP gateway to hide client IPs from app backends
item.description: OHTTP sends requests through a relay and gateway so app backends do not see client IP addresses; Cloudflare is offering a managed gateway as a paid add-on. Engineers designing privacy-sensitive services can assess a concrete deployment option.

item.title: Cloudflare K2 launches durable serverless event streams in public beta
item.description: K2 stores events as an ordered log so producers and consumers can operate independently, with consumers splitting reads or receiving all messages. The pattern addresses backpressure and downstream availability in event-driven systems.

item.title: WSL containers reaches general availability with a CLI and API
item.description: WSL containers adds a CLI for building, running and deploying Linux containers on Windows, plus an API for native Windows applications. The release expands local container workflows, including for AI workloads.

item.title: Cloud Storage SDKs enable end-to-end checksumming by default
item.description: Cloud Storage SDKs now enable end-to-end checksumming by default, building on server-side CRC32 validation and object checksums. This reduces the work needed to detect data corruption across uploads and downloads.

item.title: Google Cloud Managed Lustre adds a lower-cost tier for AI and HPC workloads
item.description: The Dynamic Tier is priced at 6 cents per GB-month and aims to keep hot data in a shared namespace with sub-millisecond latency. Consolidating storage and development workflows could reduce staging and dataset-copying toil for AI teams.

item.title: SPF authorizes senders, DKIM signs mail, and DMARC enforces alignment
item.description: The guide explains how SPF authorizes sending servers, DKIM signs messages and DMARC checks alignment and applies policy. These records are practical prerequisites for reliable automated email delivery.

item.title: Long-term memory contracts are reshaping consumer hardware supply
item.description: The article describes memory makers shifting DRAM and NAND toward longer agreements with fewer customers, while diverting supply away from consumers. Engineers planning hardware-heavy or cloud workloads should track how these supply changes affect costs and procurement.

item.title: Google Cloud adds a high-density sandbox runtime for agent workloads
item.description: Google Cloud reports that its open-source GKE Agent Substrate targets millions of sandboxes, with 10× higher density than standard container runtimes and sub-500ms resume operations. The update matters to teams evaluating infrastructure for large fleets of isolated agent workloads.

item.title: NVIDIA releases cuObject libraries and a GPU-initiated storage SDK
item.description: The generally available cuObject libraries provide APIs and an RDMA protocol for object-storage access that avoids routing data through the server CPU; the SCADA SDK supports GPU-initiated requests. These interfaces show how storage infrastructure is evolving to feed GPU workloads more directly.

item.title: GKE Agent Sandbox targets cold starts and image pulls in agentic RL
item.description: Google Cloud introduces an RL-optimized Agent Sandbox and orchestration SDK to address CPU sandbox cold starts, large image pulls and scheduling backlogs; the title claims 45× faster performance. Faster rollout infrastructure could reduce idle accelerator time in agent training and evaluation.

item.title: Stratus fault-tolerant server ran for 24 years without an unplanned shutdown
item.description: A Stratus fault-tolerant server booted in 1993 and reportedly ran without an unplanned shutdown for 24 years, with about 80% of its system original. Its redundancy and long-life maintenance offer a small-scale reliability case study.

item.title: NSL runs multiple Linux development distros in containers on one VM
item.description: NSL uses a single VM hosting systemd-nspawn containers and provides host file edits and port sharing for multiple Linux development instances. It offers an approach to isolating development environments without repeatedly changing the host installation.

item.title: Cloudflare adds per-connection visibility into post-quantum TLS adoption
item.description: Customers can inspect and graph the key-exchange algorithm negotiated on incoming TLS connections through Cloudflare logging and analytics products. This kind of telemetry helps infrastructure teams find cryptographic migration gaps.

item.title: Google Cloud Z4D instances offer up to 84,000 GiB of local SSD
item.description: The Z4D VM and bare-metal family targets IO-intensive workloads and offers up to 84,000 GiB of local SSD, with claimed performance up to 40% above Z3. The storage capacity and generation comparison may inform infrastructure choices for databases and AI workloads.

item.title: Fakecloud emulates 105 AWS services for local integration tests
item.description: Fakecloud says it supports 7,508 operations and passes all 248,557 Smithy variants, while letting applications use regular AWS clients locally. Realistic local integration tests can shorten feedback loops for teams building on AWS.

item.title: Tor hidden services expose a site without DNS or a public IP
item.description: A hidden service routes traffic to a local port using a Tor-owned directory, without DNS, a certificate authority or an exposed IP. The setup is a useful, compact example of privacy-focused network hosting.

item.title: GKE adds native scale-to-zero and capacity buffers for restarting workloads
item.description: GKE 1.37 can scale workloads to zero replicas and restart them on capacity buffers when demand returns, positioning the feature against KEDA-based setups. It offers platform teams a way to cut idle compute without abandoning responsiveness.

item.title: NVCRE isolates suspect GPU nodes by splitting failing workload groups
item.description: The open-source Kubernetes controller runs topology-aware distributed workloads and repeatedly splits failing groups to narrow down suspect nodes. That approach can make pre-production GPU cluster validation more actionable than a group-wide failure report.

item.title: NodeWright rolls out host updates across Kubernetes GPU fleets in stages
item.description: NodeWright drains nodes, applies packages, and restores them while respecting disruption budgets and workload labels; rollout policies support fixed, linear, or exponential batches. This gives operators a controlled path for host-level changes across GPU fleets.

item.title: Meta’s Petal cable targets petabit capacity across the Atlantic
item.description: Petal is planned as a roughly 7,000-kilometer cable connecting France and the United States, using multi-core fiber at scale and targeting service in 2029. Its capacity and fiber choices matter to engineers building global infrastructure.

item.title: Topograph publishes cluster topology for Kubernetes and Slurm schedulers
item.description: Topograph normalizes topology from cloud APIs and on-premises fabrics, then exposes it through Kubernetes labels, Slurm configuration, or Slinky ConfigMaps. Keeping scheduler topology current can help place AI workloads in efficient locality domains.

item.title: Tine uses Buck2 to build pinned, verifiable operating-system images
item.description: Tine is a Buck2-based build system designed to control and pin every input while reusing upstream distribution packages. Those constraints matter when building reproducible OS images that can respond quickly to CVEs.

item.title: Guix images on Linode configure disks and expand the root filesystem
item.description: The Linode image handles virtual disks in the initrd, mounts root and swap, and resizes the root filesystem to use the available volume. These boot and provisioning details are useful to engineers building reproducible cloud deployments.

item.title: Cloudflare makes Python Workers generally available
item.description: Python Workers are now a supported platform language, with FastAPI, Django and Flask support and integrations across services including Workers AI, R2 and D1. Teams can evaluate whether existing Python applications fit this serverless runtime.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37 adds a beta condition showing whether a PVC is unused
item.description: The PVC protection controller now reports an Unused condition when no running pod references a claim, avoiding custom cross-referencing to find orphaned storage. This helps cluster operators identify capacity and cloud-cost waste without risking automatic deletion.

item.title: Floci runs AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI service emulators locally
item.description: Floci offers local emulators for four cloud providers; its page reports 24 ms startup for AWS and 13 MiB idle memory for Azure, with no cloud credentials required. Local cloud APIs can speed up development and give AI agents a credential-free environment to exercise integrations.

item.title: Cloudflare Cache Rules add controls for Vary-based cache entries
item.description: Cache Rules can normalize selected request headers, pass their exact values through, or bypass caching when Vary creates too many distinct entries. These controls address the trade-off between serving correct responses and keeping caches reusable.

item.title: systemd 262 can build as a static binary for small containers
item.description: systemd 262 adds a statically linked single-binary build option for small containers, along with Linux 6.17 coredump socket support and OpenSSL 4 support. The container option is relevant to engineers working on compact runtime environments.

item.title: Cloudflare Python Workers reach general availability on Pyodide and WebAssembly
item.description: Cloudflare runs Python compiled with Pyodide in its V8-based workerd runtime, while the local tool simulates that stack in a 123 MB binary; threading and multiprocessing do not work in the WebAssembly VM. The implementation and runtime limitations help teams evaluate Python on Workers.
